record.what_it_does: Shared-inbox customer support platform with email, chat, Docs knowledge base and reports.
record.auth_notes: Mailbox API 2.0 uses OAuth2 Authorization Code (for integrations used by other users) and Client Credentials (internal). Bearer tokens; access tokens last 2 days; refresh tokens for auth code. A separate Docs API uses API keys. Multi-user toolkit would use Authorization Code.
record.access_notes: Apps are created under Your Profile > My apps. Help Scout's MCP doc says API access comes with the Standard, Plus and Pro plans, so a paid account is needed. I did not confirm whether a trial gives API access, or whether public distribution needs app review. Help Scout runs an integrations Marketplace that probably involves a listing process.
record.api_breadth_notes: Base https://api.helpscout.net/v2. Covers conversations (threads, attachments, tags, snooze, custom fields), customers, inboxes, organizations, properties, ratings, reports, users, teams, tags, webhooks and workflows. Roughly 50+ operations, estimated from the resource list rather than counted.
record.mcp_notes: https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp, hosted by Help Scout, with OAuth sign-in per user. Works with Claude and ChatGPT custom connectors. A community server also exists (drewburchfield/help-scout-mcp-server).
record.blocker_notes: The API needs a paid Help Scout plan. Whether public OAuth apps need review, and whether a free trial or sandbox exists, is unconfirmed.

evidence.quote: The Authorization Code flow is typically used for integrations to be used by other Help Scout users.
The Client Credentials flow is meant for internal integrations.
Webhooks enable Help Scout to call a script on your server when one or more events have happened.
This integration is available on the Standard, Plus, and Pro plans — any plan that includes Help Scout API access.

record.needs_human: Confirm whether a free trial or developer account gives API access. Confirm whether public OAuth apps need Help Scout review or a Marketplace listing. Check whether an OpenAPI spec or sandbox exists, and what the rate limits are. The developer docs pages I fetched did not cover these points.
